hook: The hospital needs ₹2,000 today. You can pay it back over three months, but you do not have it right now.
prompt: Four ways to get ₹2,000. Put them in order, cheapest to pay back first.
choose: Now pick the one you would actually use.
summary: You compared what each one really costs to pay back.

family.reveal: ₹2,000 back. No interest — but you owe something that is not money.
family.missed: You missed a payment. Nobody charged you anything. But your uncle asked about it in front of everyone at dinner, and that cost something too.

bnpl.reveal: ₹2,400 back. Only ₹400 a month — the smallest of the four, which is exactly why it feels cheapest. But it runs for six months, not three, and you pay ₹400 more than you would have.
bnpl.missed: You missed a payment. A ₹400 late fee was added, and it is now on your repayment record.

moneylender.reveal: ₹2,600 back. Ten percent a month: ₹200 every month, on top of the ₹2,000.
moneylender.missed: You missed a payment. The interest kept running, so you now owe more than when you started.

loan_app.reveal: ₹3,100 back, and that is if nothing goes wrong. A ₹300 processing fee, ₹400 interest, and a ₹400 penalty if you are late.
loan_app.missed: You missed a payment. The app started calling the contacts in your phone — people who had nothing to do with the loan. This is what the app wanted your contact list for.

concept.total_cost: Compare what you pay back in total, not what you pay each month. A small instalment can hide a large total.

monthly_vs_total: {monthly, rupees} a month for {months} months · {total, rupees} paid back in total

result.cheapest_first: Family was cheapest at ₹2,000. The loan app costs ₹1,100 more for the same ₹2,000.
result.emi_trap: Look at the monthly amounts again. Pay later had the smallest instalment of all four — and the second biggest total. A small monthly payment stretched over more months is not a cheaper loan.

missed_intro: Money was tight and you missed one payment.
